title: Signed URL whose expiry parameters are in the past
summary: A signed URL (any of the three providers) whose expiry parameters place it in the past.
rationale: Providers document expiry as ending validity, and AWS notes URLs also expire when the signing credential is revoked. Whether an elapsed or revoked URL should still be treated as a value to protect (it may reveal the signing identity, bucket and path, and expiry is not checkable from text alone) is a policy question, not a provider statement. Stored access policies mean the expiry may not even appear in an Azure SAS URL.

expectation.rationale: Unresolved. Sources document validity windows, not whether expired values remain sensitive. Candidate outcomes: flag regardless of expiry, or allow expiry-aware handling. A maintainer decision with a non-author reviewer would settle it; the expiry parameter alone cannot be used as ground truth. No fixture is authored.

sources.supports: A presigned URL remains valid for the period of time specified when the URL is generated.
The longest expiration value is 604800 seconds (7 days).
With a stored access policy the SAS inherits start time, expiry time and permissions from the policy.
